curated_sources.title: The Chemical Basis of Morphogenesis
curated_sources.mechanism: A spatially homogeneous state can become unstable and develop structure through reaction and transport, with small disturbances acting as triggers.
curated_sources.why_relevant: Aeterna repeatedly asks when initially weak structure becomes organized spatial structure. The paper suggests testing transport/control-timescale sensitivity rather than prescribing a target pattern.
curated_sources.translation_warning: g001 is not Turing's multi-morphogen reaction-diffusion system. The experiment below is only a mechanism-inspired perturbation, not a reproduction of the paper.

experiment_templates.question: If the local control timescale varies smoothly in space, does anonymous organization change in a reproducible way?
experiment_templates.strict_transfer_question: Without imposing a target geometry, do naturally occurring variations in local relaxation/transport timescale predict where anonymous organization appears?

curated_sources.title: Growth and division of active droplets provides a model for protocells
curated_sources.mechanism: A chemically driven material supply can make droplets grow until shape instabilities produce division-like daughter droplets.
curated_sources.why_relevant: Aeterna has relation-network separation but not biological division. This literature suggests explicitly separating growth/energy supply, shape instability and division as different questions.
curated_sources.translation_warning: A local energy pulse in g001 is not a chemically active droplet metabolism. It is an exploratory analogy used only to ask whether localized supply changes later instability.

experiment_templates.question: Does a localized supply of field amplitude create a later growth-to-instability sequence rather than merely a larger static structure?
experiment_templates.strict_transfer_question: In strict runs with no supplied target, do spontaneously growing localized structures show a size/growth threshold before independently defined instability or separation?

curated_sources.title: Kibble-Zurek mechanism and beyond in a holographic superfluid disk
curated_sources.mechanism: Crossing a continuous transition at finite rate connects quench timescales to spontaneous symmetry breaking and topological-defect production.
curated_sources.why_relevant: g001 is externally quenched and already measures winding defects. A paired slow/fast-quench experiment can test whether defect and anonymous-transition statistics depend systematically on the environmental timescale.
curated_sources.translation_warning: Matching a quench-rate trend would not establish Kibble-Zurek universality in g001. The bridge only imports the falsifiable idea that transition rate may control defect statistics.

curated_sources.title: Motility-Induced Phase Separation
curated_sources.mechanism: Persistent self-driven motion can itself generate phase separation even without ordinary attractive interactions.
curated_sources.why_relevant: It is a reminder not to interpret clustering as evidence of an attractive force. Aeterna should keep activity/drive, clustering and force claims logically separate.
curated_sources.translation_warning: g001 currently has no particle self-propulsion degree of freedom, so this source is retained as a conceptual/instrument-design source and is not auto-translated into a direct reproduction experiment.
